 When We Were Young Festival announces 2027 lineup: See Blink-182, Limp Bizkit 
 By 
 Matt Levy 
 Published 
 Nov. 18, 2026, 12:42 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make California Post a Preferred Source 
 Getty Images 
 New York Post may be compensated and/or receive an affiliate commission if you click or buy through our links. Featured pricing is subject to change.
 This should be a hot topic amongst Hot Topic fans.
 The When We Were Young Festival just announced their 2027 lineup and it’s filled to the gills with anti-authority heroes from yesteryear.
 Just five of the most notable acts headed to the Las Vegas Festival Grounds next fall on Saturday, Oct. 16, 2027, include: 
 Blink-182 
 Sophomoric yet sophisticated punk legends 
 Limp Bizkit 
 Nü metal royalty who brought the world “Nookie” 
 Pierce The Veil 
 Post-hardcore rockers with a penchant for pop melodies 
 Third Eye Blind 
 ’90s hitmakers behind timeless hits “Semi-Charmed Life” and “Jumper” 
 The Used 
 Utah’s most beloved post-hardcore screamo band 
 Advertisement
 They’ll be joined by fan favorites Circa Survive , New Found Glory, Hot Mulligan , Simple Plan and Taking Back Sunday .
 Mellower acts like Michelle Branch , Natasha Bedingfield, Ashlee Simpson, 5 Seconds of Summer and The Psychedelic Furs will be on hand as well.
 Personally, we’re most excited to see Wheatus and Reel Big Fish live on the same day, but that’s just us.
 BUY TICKETS FOR WHEN WE WERE YOUNG 2027 
 In total, over 50 acts are set to take the stage at the one-day extravaganza.
 Advertisement
 Amenities at past WWWY installments include dedicated lounges, viewing areas and cabanas for higher tiers. For our money, Shake Shack, Island Noodles, Korean corn dogs, the vegan Tacotarian, and After Eats (a vegan ice cream spot) were just a few of the most mouth-watering vendors on the premises.
 Fans had an incredible time at previous editions, too.
 “From behind the lens and in the middle of the crowd, When We Were Young 2025 felt like a perfect collision of past and present,” The Luna Collective wrote in an emphatic yet even-handed review of the festivities.
 “It was nostalgic of course, emotional but not overly curated, and just the right amount of heavy without being overbearing. The festival is clearly growing into something bigger every year—and at this rate, it’s not just honoring the scene, it’s shaping what it becomes next and keeping our inner childhood alive!”
 Advertisement
 A pre-sale begins Friday, Nov. 20 at 10 a.m. PT through Ticketmaster but general admission passes are available now on trusted secondary market sites like Vivid Seats.
 We only recommend sites with a 100% buyer guarantee, so you know your transaction is safe and your tickets will arrive on time.
